PullRequest.Title: editor: fix @vscode/diff bridge, report diff validity in telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
Follow-up to [#316990](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/316990), which added the `advanced-external` and `advanced-wasm` diff algorithms backed by `@vscode/diff`.

This PR has two parts:
1. A correctness fix for the bridge to `@vscode/diff`.
2. Telemetry on how often a diff is incorrect, so `advanced-wasm` can be rolled out with an A/B experiment.

## 1. Fix the `@vscode/diff` bridge
### Problem
The bridge in `externalLinesDiffComputer.ts` always passed `ignoreTrimWhitespace: true` to `@vscode/diff` (marked with a TODO). With that option the package's string edit drops whitespace changes, so applying it no longer reproduces the modified text. The bridge reconstructed the modified offsets by accumulating length deltas over that incomplete edit, so the offsets drifted:
- wrong inner-change highlights ([#318958](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/318958), [#317301](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/317301));
- `Assertion Failed` in `lineRangeMappingFromRangeMappings` ([#333747](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/333747); reproduced in Code OSS with the attached `repro.json`).

The pure-JS backend failed the same way, so this was not specific to wasm.

### Fix
The bridge keeps using only the public, offset-based API (`createDiffComputer` / `computeDiff`). Conversion from the string edit to line mappings happens in VS Code. This is transitional: VS Code should eventually carry offset-based diffs further and only derive line ranges where the UI needs them.
- The algorithm always diffs whitespace (`ignoreTrimWhitespace: false`), so its edit reproduces the modified text.
- `ignoreTrimWhitespace` is applied in VS Code: replacements that only touch leading/trailing whitespace of a single line (on both sides) are hidden. Whitespace changes inside a line stay visible. Modified offsets are accumulated over the full edit before filtering, so they can't drift.

This mirrors [microsoft/vscode-packages#390](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/390), which proposes removing `ignoreTrimWhitespace` from the package and annotating these replacements instead. Once that ships, `isInTrimWhitespace` can be replaced with the package's annotation.

`maxComputationTimeMs` is still not forwarded (the TODO now says why): the wasm build of the pinned 0.0.2-7 panics when measuring time (`std/src/sys/time/unsupported.rs`, observed in Code OSS). The current package source uses `Date.now()`, and a 300 ms limit stopped a 21k → 33k line diff after 327 ms. Forwarding it belongs in the package bump.

## 2. Diff validity telemetry
Different algorithms are not expected to produce the same diff, so this does not compare algorithms; performance will come from an A/B experiment on `diffEditor.diffAlgorithm`. What we need to know is how often an algorithm produces an *incorrect* diff.

- For a sample of diffs, the editor worker checks the result (`verifyLinesDiff`): applying the inner changes to the original must reproduce the modified text. When trim whitespace is ignored, lines only need to match after trimming.
  - Results: `valid`, `invalid`, or `unverified` (some change has no inner changes, e.g. `legacy`).
- **Sampling.** The check is linear in the document size. Measured: 0.6–1.4 ms for 2.2k lines, 10–18 ms for 100k lines; up to ~20% of the diff time for large files with small diffs. So it is not done for every diff:
  - the renderer requests it with the probability `diffEditor.experimental.verifyDiffSampleRate` (hidden, experiment-controlled, default 0);
  - it is never done for documents with more than 50k lines.
- `IDocumentDiff.validity` is set only for checked diffs.
- The existing `diffEditor.computeDiff` event gains `diffAlgorithm`, `ignoreTrimWhitespace` and `validity` (`notChecked` when not sampled). No content is sent.
  - Share of incorrect diffs per algorithm: `countif(validity == "invalid") / countif(validity in ("valid", "invalid"))`, grouped by `diffAlgorithm`.
  - Timing analyses should use `validity == "notChecked"` events, since `timeMs` includes the check otherwise.

This already found a bug in the built-in `advanced` algorithm. When ignoring trim whitespace, it also hides whitespace changes *inside* lines that were joined (e.g. `const response =       await …` vs `const response = await …`). It produces incorrect diffs on the `invalid-diff-bug` and `invalid-diff-trimws` fixtures. The `@vscode/diff` bridge produces valid diffs on both.

Verified in Code OSS (`advanced-wasm`, default `ignoreTrimWhitespace: true`, the [#333747](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/333747) repro): `diffEditor.computeDiff` reports `validity: notChecked` by default and `validity: valid` with `verifyDiffSampleRate: 1`.

## Behavior notes
- Without "ignore trim whitespace", the external algorithms gave the same result as `advanced` on all diffing fixtures except `invalid-ranges` (empty original). There `advanced` replaces the whole document while the string edit inserts. Both are valid, and the diff editor handles empty documents before calling any algorithm.
- With "ignore trim whitespace", inner highlights can differ slightly from `advanced`, e.g. whether leading indentation is part of a highlighted range: lines are aligned including whitespace before hiding, instead of ignoring whitespace during alignment.

## Tests
- `fixtures.test.ts`: every fixture through `advanced`, `advanced-external` and `advanced-wasm`, with and without ignoring trim whitespace. All diffs must be valid, except the two known `advanced` bugs above, which are pinned. Plus a test pinning which whitespace changes `ignoreTrimWhitespace` hides.
- New `verifyLinesDiff.test.ts`: valid, invalid and unverified diffs, with and without trimming.
- `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/editor/test/node/diffing/verifyLinesDiff.test.ts --run src/vs/editor/test/node/diffing/fixtures.test.ts`: 121 passing.
- `scripts\test.bat` with the same files: 121 passing. The electron renderer skips `advanced-wasm`, because the package's wasm loader takes its node code path there and cannot import `node:fs`.
- `npm run typecheck-client` and eslint pass.

## Manual testing
- Set `"diffEditor.diffAlgorithm": "advanced-wasm"` and compare files, for example the repro texts from [#318958](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/318958) and [#333747](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/333747). They render without assertion errors.
- Correct highlights for non-ASCII text (emoji, CJK) additionally need the wasm fix from [microsoft/vscode-packages#389](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/389) and a package bump.
- Telemetry: set `"diffEditor.experimental.verifyDiffSampleRate": 1`, start with `--log trace`, open a diff, and check `telemetry.log` for `diffEditor.computeDiff` with `validity`.

Related: [#318958](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/318958), [#317301](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/317301), [#333747](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/333747)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added critical-path call, full-text allocations, force-large-model synchronization, and ineffective line-only bound are directly traced. Exact latency varies by file size and sampling rate, but the mechanism and realistic long-line trigger are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and document-sized strings/arrays allocated while reconstructing and comparing the texts
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Once sampled, cost grows with total character count, not line count; a one-line or otherwise low-line-count generated file can be tens of megabytes and still pass both 50,000-line checks.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Sampled large diffs remain on the diff editor critical path longer and create substantial transient memory/GC pressure before the result can render.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, a cache-miss diff returned after the configured diff algorithm completed; it did not reconstruct and compare the entire output text for telemetry.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: For every sampled cache miss under 50,000 lines, the worker now calls `verifyLinesDiff` before returning. That function materializes an applied result, joins the entire modified document (or splits and trims the applied result), so low-line-count large files receive additional full-document work.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `_shouldVerify` guard at lines 184-185 enables verification based only on each model's line count, while the same diff adds the worker-side call to `verifyLinesDiff`; no character-count bound is applied.
Findings.Title: [medium] Bound sampled verification by character count
Findings.Impact: With the experiment enabled, opening or editing a diff of a large minified bundle, generated JSON, or another file with very long lines can add large full-text copies and linear scans after diff computation. The caller awaits this same worker request before rendering, and diff model synchronization explicitly forces large models, so the line limit does not protect this scenario.
Findings.Evidence: `computeDiff` calls `_shouldVerify` on each cache miss and awaits the worker. The new guard checks only `getLineCount()`. In `EditorWorker.computeDiff`, a true flag synchronously calls `verifyLinesDiff`; `verifyLinesDiff` calls `edit.normalize().apply(...)` and then either `modifiedLines.join('\n')` or `actual.split('\n')` plus per-line trim. `EditorWorkerService.computeDiff` uses `_workerWithResources(..., true)`, bypassing the model's 50 MB synchronization limit, and the view model awaits this result on its render/update path.
Findings.Recommendation: Add a total-character/byte bound using the models' value lengths (in addition to the line bound) before sampling, sized to the telemetry budget; skip verification when either model or their combined size exceeds it.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The repeated boundary scans and awaited call path are explicit. The exact replacement count depends on `@vscode/diff`, but the tests establish separate intra-line mappings and isolated whitespace edits are a realistic high-cardinality input.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU string searches and substring/regular-expression work in the editor worker
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For k whitespace-only replacements on a line of length L, each call performs `lastIndexOf` and `indexOf` searches to the line boundaries, making the new filtering stage O(k×L) on a long single line rather than proportional to the document plus edit ranges.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: External/wasm diff results can be delayed by repeated multi-megabyte scans, reducing worker throughput and making the diff editor wait before rendering.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Previously the adapter passed `ignoreTrimWhitespace: true` into `@vscode/diff` and only converted the replacements returned by the package; it did not rescan the containing source and target lines for each replacement.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The PR always asks the package to diff whitespace, then classifies each whitespace-only replacement in the adapter. Classification repeatedly searches from the edit to both ends of its containing line in both original and modified text.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `isInTrimWhitespace` implementation computes both line boundaries with `lastIndexOf`/`indexOf` for every candidate replacement at lines 109-111, and the added loop call at line 74 invokes it while filtering edits.
Findings.Title: [medium] Avoid rescanning an entire long line for every whitespace edit
Findings.Impact: With `ignoreTrimWhitespace` enabled, a realistic minified bundle or generated single-line JSON file containing many isolated whitespace edits causes the post-diff adapter to scan the same very long line once per edit. This runs inside the awaited worker request after the external diff has already completed and can add seconds of CPU for sufficiently large lines/edit counts.
Findings.Evidence: The loop processes every external replacement. `isInTrimWhitespace` first confirms a whitespace-only range, then unconditionally calls `text.lastIndexOf('\n', range.start - 1)` and `text.indexOf('\n', range.endExclusive)` before testing the prefix/suffix. The added fixture demonstrates that isolated intra-line whitespace differences remain separate replacement mappings, so replacement cardinality can grow independently within one line. The diff view awaits this worker call; cache hits avoid it, but every changed model version is a cache miss.
Findings.Recommendation: Classify trim whitespace with bounded scans outward from the range that stop at the first non-whitespace character or newline (or precompute line boundaries once and reuse them), so total filtering work is proportional to text/edit size rather than rescanning the containing line per replacement.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or recompute a diff while the experimental validity sample selects the computation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On an exact-version cache miss, the diff view awaits model synchronization and one worker `computeDiff` request; the changed worker now completes `verifyLinesDiff` after the algorithm and before returning, so verification is directly on the render/update critical path. Telemetry transport itself is off the critical path after local event enqueueing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize original and modified model contents into the editor worker on first use or after updates
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to two model synchronization messages for a cold pair, then incremental model-change messages while models remain synchronized
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same forced large-model synchronization occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold synchronization must reach the worker before computation; warm synchronized models avoid full resend

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request and return one document diff computation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per diff-cache miss after the 200 ms edit coalescing; the added verify flag is a scalar on the existing request
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request returned immediately after diff computation and result conversion, without full-text validity verification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The caller awaits the response before publishing the rendered diff, and verification now extends this request when sampled

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Eventually transmit the existing `diffEditor.computeDiff` telemetry event through telemetry batching
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing event per completed cache-miss computation; the PR adds three scalar fields but no additional event
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The event already existed with timing, timeout, and move measurements.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only local telemetry enqueueing occurs in this method; transport is not required for diff rendering

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One verification per sampled cache-miss computation. Effective size is total characters plus inner-change count, despite admission being based only on each model having at most 50,000 lines; generated/minified files can therefore contain tens or hundreds of megabytes under the limit.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Content edits are coalesced by a 200 ms scheduler, but an already-running worker computation is not interrupted by the cancellation token. Worker-side verification is synchronous on the worker event loop, so it blocks later work handled by that worker rather than gaining parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An exact URI/model-version/options hit in the static diff cache returns before sampling and incurs no worker or verification work. Every changed version is a miss; sampled results are then cached like other results. There is no separate verification cache or negative state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the line-only guard, forced synchronization of large models, synchronous full-text reconstruction/comparison, and awaited worker response are all explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The experiment-controlled sample rate defaults to zero and deployed rates are unknown; exact pauses and GC depend on model size. The long-line admission gap and full-document allocations are certain when sampled.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable serialization/allocation regression: the intended large-document safeguard measures lines while the added work scales with characters, allowing sampled long-line files to add large critical-path CPU and transient memory.

Scenarios.Scenario: Compute an `advanced-external` or `advanced-wasm` diff with ignore-trim-whitespace enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a diff-cache miss, the view awaits worker resolution of the external computer, external diff computation, the changed per-replacement trim-whitespace filter, line mapping conversion, and the IPC response. The filter is therefore on the visible diff critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize models and invoke one editor-worker diff computation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worker request per cache miss, plus cold/incremental model synchronization as above
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same worker boundary existed, but its adapter did not perform per-replacement line-boundary rescans.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The view awaits the worker response; the changed CPU filtering happens inside this boundary before response

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dynamically load the `@vscode/diff` module and initialize the selected JS/wasm computer
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per worker/module lifetime for module load and once per `useWasm` boolean for computer creation due promise caches
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The module and JS/wasm computers were already loaded and promise-cached separately.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold first use waits for initialization; warm uses reuse the cached computer

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective multiplicity is the number of whitespace-only replacement edits returned for each containing line. For k isolated replacements on a line of length L, the new boundary searches can rescan that line O(k×L); minified bundles and one-line generated JSON provide realistic large L and k.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Computations execute synchronously within the editor worker event loop. The UI remains responsive, but this request and later worker tasks wait; rapid edits are debounced but do not cancel work already executing in the worker.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Exact model-version/options cache hits bypass the worker. On misses, the external module and one computer per wasm boolean are promise-cached, so module initialization is cold-only; filtering runs for every changed diff and has no per-line preprocessing cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: each whitespace candidate invokes the added helper, and that helper searches backward and forward to line boundaries before checking trim position; the fixture proves multiple independent mappings can exist within a line.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact edit coalescing by the external package and machine-specific string-search throughput determine duration. The added per-edit scans and long-single-line trigger are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression: adapter-side trim filtering can repeatedly scan the same very long line once per isolated whitespace edit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Compute ordinary unsampled diffs and emit enriched performance telemetry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing diff algorithm and worker IPC remain the critical path. When sampling does not select the computation, the verify flag is false and no validity reconstruction runs. Added telemetry consists of scalar metadata enqueued after the worker response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing editor-worker diff request with one added optional boolean and one optional scalar response field
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request omitted the verification flag/validity field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Payload growth is constant and negligible; no additional boundary call

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing telemetry event receives algorithm, whitespace option, and validity scalars
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per completed cache miss, unchanged
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One event with three fewer scalar properties was emitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Event enqueueing is local and transport is off the diff critical path

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One configuration lookup/random draw and three scalar telemetry fields per diff-cache miss; no dependence on document collection size beyond existing diff work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing 200 ms recomputation coalescing and worker execution behavior are unchanged. Telemetry upload remains externally batched by the existing telemetry service.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Exact diff-cache hits return before both sampling and telemetry, as before. External computer promise caches preserve one computer per backend.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that unsampled behavior adds only constant metadata/configuration work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Telemetry serializer implementation was not changed; any byte increase is a few scalar fields and does not scale with content.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate performance finding: the unchanged event and IPC cardinality receive only bounded scalar metadata.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and all diff hunks. Traced diff-view scheduling, cache behavior, worker synchronization/IPC, external module lifecycle, verification allocations, telemetry, and external whitespace filtering. Submitted two medium-confidence-or-higher actionable regressions: character-unbounded sampled verification and repeated long-line rescans per whitespace edit.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
